feat.name: Toxicologist
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Potent Poisons
entries: When you deal damage to a creature with a poison, the damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the poison's damage type.

entries.name: Precise Chemist
entries: You gain {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB} with the {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}. When you {@variantrule Crafting Poisons|Starlight|craft a poison}, you can add a catalyst to it, which does one of the following without affecting the rarity, cost, or time to make the poison:

entries.name: Highly Concentrated
entries: Increase the DC of the poison by 2.

entries.name: Potent Formulation
entries: Increase the damage by one rarity (if the poison is Legendary: {@dice 1d12} becomes {@dice 2d6}, {@dice 11d6} becomes {@dice 13d6}).

entries.name: Careful Dosage
entries: Double the duration of the poison's effect, the duration of the coating, or the number of pieces of ammunition coated.

variantrule.name: Crafting Poisons
entries: {@note Crafting a poison requires {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB} with a {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}.
When crafting a poison, you choose whether it is a weapon coating or a single-use poison as the 'base', also deciding the delivery mechanism.

Then you add an agent, which determines the poison's rarity (and thus the power) and potential effect(s) of the poison: this may be a {@variantrule Monster Components|Starlight|component from a monster}, magic from a spell or class feature, or a similar valuable item.

Crafting time does not need to be done continuously - a poison might be a simple mixing of ingredients, or require time to settle, mix, distill, dissolve, and so on. This could be done while the poison remains in your bag, but only one can be made at a time with each {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}.
The bases are as follows: Weapon coating (Contact or Injury); Single-Use (Injury, Contact, Inhaled, Ingested, or Cloud).
The rarity of the agent influences the damage and save DC of the poison. A Single-Use poison will often do 4-6x as much damage as a Coating poison of the same rarity, but can only be used once.

If the poison inflicts a condition, lower its damage by one rarity. For example a Rare Remorhaz tooth could provide a {@dice 1d8} Fire weapon coating, or a {@dice 1d6} Fire Weapon coating that has a DC 15 saving throw against Burning. Or a Single-Use poison that does {@dice 5d6} Fire damage with the same saving throw.

A poison might inflict its damage over a longer period of time or after a delay - consider the full damage when determining rarity, but if the period is extremely long (such as an hour or more) a creature is likely to have time to cure the poison before suffering much of its effect. If damage is inflicted on every saving throw, increase the potential damage by one tier, as it is unlikely the full damage will ever be applied!

If a poison inflicts more than one condition (such as {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} and a secondary condition that depends on being Poisoned), consider this as two conditions and lower the damage accordingly. This is a reasonable way to ugprade an existing poison. If a poison inflicts two negative effects (such as the {@item Oil of Diminution|Starlight}), count those separately.

If a poison does no damage and inflicts a condition, the condition could be quite unique or powerful (see {@item Phantasmal Effluvium|Starlight} or {@item Truth Serum|Starlight}), and this will usually be Rare (but not always, see {@item Fever's Peak|Starlight}).

At the DM's discretion or player's request, the die size could be increased or decreased - the examples in this supplement use a range of dice sizes. If you're unsure, use the average value for the rarity (for example, {@dice 3d6} averages to 10, {@dice 2d10} averages to 11) - a couple of points of damage won't make a meaningful difference to power, but can change the feeling a lot; a smaller number of larger dice will roll high and low more often.

variantrule.name: Monster Components
entries: To craft any manner of magic item, potion, or poison, you may require a special component or a spell. Typically, groups of creatures are associated with certain characteristics, though some are much broader than others. An item acquired from a creature (such as a devil's horn, or a beast's tooth) might be usable to create an item fitting one of these categories.

The 'rarity' of a given component can be linked to the monster's {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} (CR): 0-5, common; 6-10, uncommon; 11-15, rare; 16-20, very rare; 21+, legendary. Legendary Actions or similar special properties could increase the rarity of an item from a monster.

Components should require some amount of effort to harvest, you may be required to make an ability check: Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}), or Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}); alternatively, using a {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB} if you are proficient with it. The DC should be based off of the monster's CR, but higher difficulty checks (or larger monsters!) could come with additional components. This can be an alternative way to a nearby treasure chest for the DM to provide reward for slaying a challenging monster.

These components could then be used for crafting or selling. As a guideline, components should sell for approximately 10 x CR x rarity (where common is 1, and legendary is 5), with a minimum of 5gp. Some components may take effort to sell for their higher value, requiring (as example), {@skill Insight|XPHB}, {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}, {@skill Survival|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, or {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Investigation|XPHB} and some number of days to locate and convince suitable and trustworthy buyers. If a monster drops several components, this could be quite a lot of gold!

Below is a table of common associations for types of monsters. It includes damage types, conditions, special features, spellcasting if applicable, and common ability scores. An individual creature may not fit this trend, at which point the categories of a component can be changed as desired (typically, a given item could be used for a couple of these categories, not any of them).
